featured_reviews.name: ashok mukherjee
featured_reviews.review_text:
Happy experience...
Thanks doctors....

Yes my friends,
People write many nasty experience they face in hospital or with doctors. Very few write their sweet experiences in hospital or with doctors.

So I thought to share my excellent sweet experience with a small, faraway hospital but with exceptional expertise in the field of knee replacement and other orthopedic and neurological complication.

My wife Operated for knee replacement on 15th...At 11 in the morning (to 2.30 pm) including recovery time inside operation theatre...

Then shifted to ICU.
Operation was good, my wife was in jolly mood and smiling while coming out from OT after the replacement ... But after 2 hrs of shifting to ICU, the real pain started... Wife was crying like mad for pain... But through medication by 8 pm it has started reducing... and she slept.
Nxt day, 16th, morning no pain...and shifted to pvt room cabin. I also staying in the same room with her. Excellent clean cosy room with all necessary requirements like AC, TV, eye catching view from 4th floor Window, attached very clean bath (no balcony), clean and daily fresh linen.

17th.. Sr Doctors and physiotherapist started her to walk and bent the new knee to 90°...

This was regular exercise, bending knee to 90° and walking in the corridor with the help of walker and physiotherapist till 19th...

And on 19th all bandage and all drain-pipes ( 3 in total... For Blood to drain our excess blood at operated knee, one for urine, one at spinal joint to push different medicine ) removed and....
discharged in the afternoon by doctor...
Same day, 19th, came to home by evening.

She is recovering nicely.... Walking inside the flat with the help of walker... pain she feel very very rarely.

After 9th day from operation, today (24th March) was the first check up...and it is absolutely OK.
Infact, my wife walk through out the day in hospital alone with the help of walker.
Today, she has been allowed by doctor to move and do morning/evening walk with walker and asked for further check up after 15 days.
No medicine given except multivitamin for further recovery as she has no pain.

We are very very happy for the excellent smooth operation, expertise of doctors, quick recovery process with effective treatment, support of Jr. Doctors, Physiotherapist, Metron, Sisters, Brothers, room boy and aayas for 24×7 and overall management of the hospital.

Well behaved people....
No extra billing...

We, and no one, before surgery, expected that after operation on 2nd day pain would vanish... she would walk and bend knee to 90°and get discharge on 4th day...!!!

All credit goes to Dr. Rahul Bade and his team including Anesthesists Dr. Ganesh Kolhe at Sparsh Multi-Speciality Hospital.

Thank you...well done, doctor !!!
🙏🙏🙏

Thanks to Lt. Col Dr Amogh Yadav from Mumbai and Dr. Rahul Mane for strongly recomanding us the hospital.

(Note : Treatment was going on at Sanchiti Hospital. But operated at Sparsh Multi Speciality Hospital)

featured_reviews.review_text:
The care given is really good.
My mother was admitted here. They give personalized attention and good care.
The doctors are well experienced, attentive and explain you everything properly.
The staff is very helpful when it comes to solving any problem.
You are not allowed to get your food. So, if you are a patient's relative, as a local guide I would suggest don't fall for canteen food. The canteen food mostly offers biscuits and stuff like misal pav vada. 1-2 protein bars which are processed.

There is a seperate menu from which you can order food which offers options like Khichadi and dahi which are decent.
Because, when your relatives is admitted in the hospital neglecting your own health and falling for sugary oily food may not be a good option.

I would suggest they have seperate menu, which you will need to call a number and ask for, there you get better options than the processed food.

There is personalised dietician assigned to each patient. She mostly gives balanced options for the patients. I had seen Marie Biscuit in my mom's diet. I personally don't want my mom to eat biscuits with palm oil in it. So, she switched the snack.
So, if you have special preferences. You can always communicate.

One more suggestion to the hospital.
If you have a room patient's relative mostly gets assigned bed.
But if the patient is in the ICU there is no assigned bed for the patient's relative. Which is mostly offered in some other hospitals. So, that could be added.

⭐ Very Disappointing Experience – Not Recommended for Delivery Cases

I had trusted Shatabdi Hospital for years — my father-in-law and mother were admitted here before, and we always believed it was a reliable municipal hospital. But this time, when I went for my pregnancy check-up in my 9th month, my experience was extremely upsetting.

The OPD doctors lack basic respect and communication skills. Instead of guiding patients with care, they speak very rudely, as if they just want to finish their duty. The way they talk to pregnant women is unacceptable.

Despite being a municipal hospital where people seek help with hope, I was treated without dignity. They created unnecessary chaos during my check-up and used language that no patient should have to hear.

To avoid admitting me, they simply checked my blood pressure and weight and declared me a “high risk” patient. I was advised to go to Cooper Hospital or Nair Hospital — their exact words were that Shatabdi Hospital:

➡️ Doesn’t have an OT bed that can take a patient weighing 90 kg or above
➡️ Doesn’t have an anaesthetist capable of handling such patients

This is shocking — how can such a well-known BMC hospital openly say they don’t have facilities for patients over a certain weight? Does that mean only slim patients under 70 kg deserve treatment here?
